Welcome to the House

Welcome to House of Musa, Oluwadoyinsolami Kore Dare-Olude.

Welcome, Kore. You are joining as our Integrated Creative & Brand Lead, the role that holds brand strategy, creative direction, content, and social under one hand. This onboarding takes about fifteen minutes. We go one step at a time, in order, and by the end you will have signed your NDA and your engagement agreement, received your House of Musa email and team access, and seen your deliverables, your first 90 days, and the one year outlook mapped out.

Spread the Gold.

Know the brand

About House of Musa

House of Musa is a luxury eyewear and apparel brand rooted in the legacy of Mansa Musa. It is built on reclamation and royalty as the default: gold is not an accent here, it is the standard. The house operates across Washington DC, Atlanta, and South Africa, and it is scaling fast.

The runwayHouse of Musa frames and apparel, shown live.
The showsFashion week presentations are a core stage for the house.

What we make

Designer eyewear, named for African cities. Every frame carries a city name and a story: Kumasi, Victoria, Madina, Pretoria, Angola, and more. Frames are the front of the house, worn first and photographed close.

Clothing, starting with SS01. The first clothing collection pairs a sky blue pinstripe cropped jacket with wide leg indigo jeans, alongside tees and the Timbuktu silk scarf. Eyewear leads, clothing extends the world.

House rule worth learning on day one: the product is always the hero. Content leads with the frames, close enough to see them clearly.

Kumasi SlimBlack frame, black lenses. Shown here on white, as all product shots are.
Kumasi Slim, wornThe same frame on a face, so the fit and scale read instantly.

Where you sit

Your role: Integrated Creative & Brand Lead

This role combines brand strategy, creative direction, content strategy, styling consultation, and social media oversight. Its objective is to strengthen House of Musa’s positioning as a luxury eyewear brand, create a consistent and recognisable brand world, and build a digital presence that attracts and converts customers beyond the founder’s immediate network.

The role at a glance

  • Full time, Monday to Friday: the role averages about 40 hours per week, some weeks less and some weeks more, and the average is what counts. It is your primary professional commitment, not a part time or side arrangement.
  • Probation period: the first 3 months of the engagement are a probation period.
  • Fully remote, strategic and creative: planning, direction, coordination, review, and agreed social media management.
  • You lead a team: you manage the day to day of the people working under you, including your Personal Assistant, and coordinate and direct their work.
  • Your duties are not limited to the listed tasks: the deliverables at Step 5 are the core of the role, and you will also take on other tasks reasonably assigned as the brand’s needs require.
  • Pay: ₦560,000 per month, payable in advance at the beginning of each month. Full terms are in your agreement at Step 10.

Your standing work

Your deliverables and tasks

Everything in your proposal is built into this step, and it is also written into your agreement at Step 10. These are your core responsibilities and monthly deliverables. They are the core of the role, not its limit: you also manage the day to day of your team and take on other tasks reasonably assigned as the brand’s needs require.

Brand positioning and management

  • Translate the brand’s vision into clear positioning, messaging, and a recognisable luxury identity.
  • Clarify the brand’s target customer, lifestyle, purchasing power, product value, and reasons to choose House of Musa.
  • Develop and maintain brand voice, storytelling principles, and visual consistency across customer touchpoints.
  • Review the customer journey and identify opportunities to improve trust, product understanding, and conversion.
  • Provide strategic recommendations informed by brand performance, audience response, and market observations.

Content strategy and creative direction

  • Establish content pillars and a monthly content direction aligned with the brand’s objectives.
  • Develop monthly content calendars, campaign concepts, creative briefs, and storytelling angles.
  • Direct the visual treatment of content, including framing, product presentation, styling, mood, locations, and model direction.
  • Ensure that eyewear remains the hero product and that content communicates craftsmanship, design, quality, and the brand’s definition of luxury.
  • Review content before publication to maintain consistency in tone, quality, and visual identity.

Full content production

  • You lead full content production end to end: concept, planning, shoot direction, coordination, and delivery of finished content for the agreed platforms, working with your PA and team.
  • Budget rule: where a production task needs budget to complete it, for example crew, location, models, props, wardrobe, or equipment, you ask the founder for that budget first, with the amount and what it covers. Do not commit or spend production money until the budget is approved. Production budget is separate from your monthly pay.
  • Plan production into the monthly calendar so budget requests come early, not at the last minute.

Social media management

  • Oversee the brand’s agreed social platforms, expected to include Instagram and TikTok.
  • Plan and schedule agreed posts, write captions and calls to action, and ensure content is published according to the calendar.
  • Coordinate agreed story content and maintain consistency in community-facing communication.
  • Monitor comments and direct messages during agreed working hours and escalate customer-service or order issues to House of Musa.
  • Prepare a concise monthly performance report with observations and recommendations.

Styling and creative consultation

  • Provide styling direction for product campaigns, editorials, and social content.
  • Recommend wardrobe, accessories, colour stories, model presentation, and visual references that support the brand identity.
  • Develop creative concepts for product launches, campaign shoots, and brand storytelling.
  • Advise on how products should be presented so that the frames, details, fit, and finish are clearly visible.

Team leadership and your Personal Assistant

  • Manage the day to day of your team: set their tasks, coordinate and direct the people working under you, and review their output before it reaches the founder.
  • House of Musa provides you with a Personal Assistant who works at your direction on role-related work. Directing the PA day to day is part of managing your team.
  • Bring your team’s shipped work, blockers, and next steps to the weekly Wednesday meeting.

One year outlook, holiday and deal content, and clothing drops

  • Own the rolling one year outlook at Step 12: a directional view of the year ahead, not a locked list of everything that will go out, so the house is always ahead of the curve.
  • Holiday content and deal content always go out. Every holiday gets product led content, an email, and a deal, planned weeks ahead, never at the last minute. A standing monthly deal or promotion runs alongside them.
  • Plan the clothing drops. One collection drop per quarter, starting with the first clothing launch of select items by December 2026. You build the campaign concept, content runway, and launch calendar for each drop.
  • Keep the monthly calendar looking at least 60 days ahead, and firm the outlook up quarter by quarter at the monthly strategy meeting.

Your monthly deliverables

Strategy meetingOne monthly strategy and planning meeting.
Content calendarOne monthly content calendar for the agreed platforms.
One year outlookA rolling one year outlook, reviewed monthly: holiday content, deal content, and clothing drop planning kept at least a quarter ahead of today.
Holiday and deal contentFor every holiday: a product led content series, an email, and a deal, planned ahead with the monthly deal or promotion.
Feed postsApproximately 12 to 16 feed posts per month across the agreed platforms, using approved and supplied assets; formats and platform adaptations agreed in the calendar.
StoriesApproximately 12 to 20 story frames or story updates per month, planned around campaigns, product education, and brand activity.
Creative directionA monthly creative direction document or briefs for planned campaigns and shoots.
Full content productionEnd to end production of the month’s planned content, led by you. Where a task needs budget to complete it, you request that budget from the founder in advance and proceed once it is approved.
Campaign conceptsUp to two campaign or shoot concepts per month, including styling and visual references.
Publishing and communityCaptions, calls to action, scheduling and publishing, and agreed community management.
Performance summaryOne monthly performance summary with practical recommendations.

These quantities are planning estimates, confirmed against the final content volume, platform requirements, and the quality and quantity of assets supplied. Additional campaigns, urgent requests, or deliverables outside this list are agreed in writing before work begins.

Files, production, and editing: how it works

House of Musa provides the raw materials the role requires: original product photographs, raw video footage, product details, campaign information, brand assets, logos, approved fonts and brand guidelines, and product availability, in usable quality, correctly labelled where possible, delivered by the agreed monthly content deadlines through a shared folder or other agreed method.

Your monthly pay covers content strategy, creative direction, full content production leadership, planning, coordination, copy and captions, publishing oversight, and review of supplied assets. Full content production is part of your role. Production costs themselves are not in your pay: where a task needs budget to complete it, ask the founder for the budget first and wait for approval before committing any spend. Hands-on video editing is simply not included in the monthly pay. Full terms are in the agreement at Step 10.

The gate

Sign the NDA

This step unlocks your House of Musa email. Read and sign the one-way non-disclosure and ownership agreement below, and your @houseofmusa.store address is issued on the very next page. No NDA, no email, no Drive access. This is a one-way agreement: it protects House of Musa only, and everything you create here stays at House of Musa.

House of Musa work involves unreleased collections, supplier terms, pricing, and campaign plans. This is the full agreement, not a summary. It is one-way: the obligations are yours, and House of Musa takes on no reciprocal confidentiality obligation to you under it. Anything created at or for House of Musa belongs to House of Musa and stays at House of Musa. Read all of it, check each acknowledgment separately, then sign with your full legal name.

ONE-WAY NON-DISCLOSURE AND OWNERSHIP AGREEMENT

This Agreement is between Musa Group LLC, doing business as House of Musa (“House of Musa”), and the undersigned individual (“Recipient”), effective on the date Recipient signs below. It applies to employees, interns, contractors, creators, and suppliers engaged by House of Musa.

1. One-way agreement. House of Musa will share Confidential Information and work materials with Recipient so Recipient can do their work. This Agreement protects House of Musa only. It places obligations on Recipient and gives Recipient no rights in anything House of Musa shares or anything Recipient creates for House of Musa. House of Musa takes on no confidentiality or other obligation to Recipient under this Agreement.

2. What counts as Confidential Information. Everything Recipient sees, hears, receives, or creates through their work that is not public, including: unreleased designs, collections, tech packs, patterns, and samples; supplier, factory, and manufacturer identities, contacts, and pricing; wholesale and retail pricing strategy; customer, client, and partner lists and their contact details and order history; sales figures, revenue, budgets, and financial information; marketing plans, campaign concepts, launch dates, and ad account data; brand imagery, footage, and content before release; business plans and expansion plans; and personal information about the founder, team members, clients, and customers.

3. Recipient’s obligations. Recipient will: (a) keep all Confidential Information strictly confidential and disclose it to no one outside House of Musa; (b) use it only to do their House of Musa work, and for no personal or outside purpose; (c) not copy, photograph, record, download, or remove Confidential Information except as their role requires; (d) not post, share, or hint at unreleased products, designs, campaigns, or business information on any personal or public channel, including social media, group chats, and portfolios, without written approval from House of Musa; (e) protect any device, account, or document holding Confidential Information with reasonable care, and report any loss or suspected exposure immediately.

4. Everything created here stays at House of Musa. Everything Recipient creates, contributes to, or produces in connection with House of Musa, including designs, garments, content, copy, photographs, video, edits, strategies, documents, data, contact lists, and account content, is a work made for hire and the sole and exclusive property of Musa Group LLC from the moment it is created. To the extent any right does not vest automatically, Recipient assigns all rights, title, and interest in it to Musa Group LLC, and will sign anything reasonably needed to confirm that ownership. Recipient may not take, keep, copy, remove, use, display (including in any portfolio), sell, license, or recreate any of it, during the engagement or after it ends, without written approval from House of Musa. Work created for House of Musa stays at House of Musa.

5. Accounts and access. Anything created or stored in House of Musa accounts, drives, and systems belongs to House of Musa. Recipient’s access is a licence to do their work only, and it ends when the engagement ends or whenever House of Musa revokes it.

6. No circumvention. Recipient will not use Confidential Information to contact House of Musa’s suppliers, manufacturers, clients, customers, or partners for their own benefit, for a competing business, or on behalf of anyone else, during their engagement and for twelve (12) months after it ends.

7. How long this lasts. The confidentiality obligations begin on the date Recipient signs, cover information received before signing if it was shared in expectation of engagement, and continue for three (3) years after Recipient’s engagement ends for any reason. Information that qualifies as a trade secret stays protected for as long as it remains secret. The ownership terms in sections 4 and 5 are permanent and survive the end of the engagement.

8. Return of materials. When the engagement ends, or whenever House of Musa asks, Recipient will promptly return or permanently delete all Confidential Information and House of Musa property in their possession, including copies on personal devices and accounts, and confirm the return or deletion in writing if asked.

9. If this Agreement is broken. Recipient understands that a breach may cause harm that money alone cannot repair, and that House of Musa may seek a court order stopping further disclosure or use, in addition to any other remedies available under law.

10. General. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the District of Columbia. It is the entire agreement between the parties about Confidential Information and ownership of work created for House of Musa, and replaces any earlier understanding on those subjects. If any part is held unenforceable, the rest still applies. Signing electronically, including typing Recipient’s full legal name and the date below, counts as Recipient’s signature.

ENGAGEMENT AGREEMENT: INTEGRATED CREATIVE & BRAND LEAD

This Engagement Agreement (“Agreement”) is between House of Musa (Musa Group LLC) (“House of Musa”) and the undersigned (“Brand Lead”), for the role of Integrated Creative & Brand Lead. The Brand Lead’s Integrated Creative & Brand Lead proposal forms part of this Agreement; where this Agreement and the proposal differ, this Agreement governs.

1. Role overview. The role combines brand strategy, creative direction, content strategy, styling consultation, and social media oversight. Its objective is to strengthen House of Musa’s positioning as a luxury eyewear brand, create a consistent and recognisable brand world, and build a digital presence that attracts and converts customers beyond the founder’s immediate network. This is a fully remote, strategic and creative role covering planning, direction, coordination, review, and agreed social media management.

2. Full-time role. This is a full-time role. You work full time for House of Musa, Monday to Friday, averaging about 40 hours per week. Some weeks will be less and some weeks will be more, and the average is what counts. This engagement is your primary professional commitment for its term. It is not a part-time engagement, a freelance side arrangement, or a retainer for occasional hours.

3. Probation period. The first 3 months of this engagement are a probation period. During probation, both sides assess fit, workload, and working rhythm. The scope, workload, and pay review at the three month mark under the Term clause of this Agreement takes place at the end of the probation period.

4. Core responsibilities. Brand positioning and management: translate the brand’s vision into clear positioning, messaging, and a recognisable luxury identity; clarify the target customer, lifestyle, purchasing power, product value, and reasons to choose House of Musa; develop and maintain brand voice, storytelling principles, and visual consistency across customer touchpoints; review the customer journey and identify opportunities to improve trust, product understanding, and conversion; and provide strategic recommendations informed by brand performance, audience response, and market observations.

Content strategy and creative direction: establish content pillars and a monthly content direction; develop monthly content calendars, campaign concepts, creative briefs, and storytelling angles; direct the visual treatment of content, including framing, product presentation, styling, mood, locations, and model direction; ensure eyewear remains the hero product and content communicates craftsmanship, design, quality, and the brand’s definition of luxury; and review content before publication for consistency in tone, quality, and visual identity.

Social media management: oversee the brand’s agreed social platforms, expected to include Instagram and TikTok; plan and schedule agreed posts; write captions and calls to action and ensure content is published according to the calendar; coordinate agreed story content and maintain consistency in community-facing communication; monitor comments and direct messages during agreed working hours and escalate customer-service or order issues to House of Musa; and prepare a concise monthly performance report with observations and recommendations.

Styling and creative consultation: provide styling direction for product campaigns, editorials, and social content; recommend wardrobe, accessories, colour stories, model presentation, and visual references that support the brand identity; develop creative concepts for product launches, campaign shoots, and brand storytelling; and advise on how products should be presented so the frames, details, fit, and finish are clearly visible.

5. Monthly deliverables. One monthly strategy and planning meeting; one monthly content calendar for the agreed platforms; approximately 12 to 16 feed posts per month across the agreed platforms, using approved and supplied assets, with formats and platform adaptations agreed in the calendar; approximately 12 to 20 story frames or story updates per month, planned around campaigns, product education, and brand activity; a monthly creative direction document or briefs for planned campaigns and shoots; up to two campaign or shoot concepts per month, including styling and visual references; captions, calls to action, scheduling and publishing, and agreed community management; and one monthly performance summary with practical recommendations. The Brand Lead also leads full content production end to end for the planned monthly content: concept, planning, shoot direction, coordination, and delivery. The Brand Lead will also maintain a rolling one year outlook for the brand: a directional view of the year ahead covering holiday content, deal content, and clothing drop planning (one collection drop per quarter), reviewed at the monthly strategy meeting and firmed up quarter by quarter in the monthly content calendar. The outlook sets direction and timing; it does not lock specific products, prices, or post dates. Every holiday will have product led content, an email, and a deal planned in advance, alongside a standing monthly deal or promotion. These quantities are planning estimates, confirmed against the final content volume, platform requirements, and the quality and quantity of assets supplied. Additional campaigns, urgent requests, or deliverables outside this list will be quoted separately before work begins.

6. Duties are not limited to the listed tasks. The responsibilities and deliverables above are the core of the role, not its limit. The Brand Lead’s duties are not limited to the tasks listed in the proposal or in this Agreement. She will also manage the day to day of her team, coordinate and direct the people working under her, and take on other tasks reasonably assigned by House of Musa as the brand’s needs require.

7. Personal Assistant. House of Musa will provide the Brand Lead with a Personal Assistant to support her in carrying out this role. The Personal Assistant works at the Brand Lead’s direction on role-related work, and the Brand Lead is responsible for the Personal Assistant’s day to day direction as part of managing her team.

8. Content files, production, and editing. House of Musa is responsible for providing the raw materials the role requires: original product photographs, raw video footage, product details, campaign information, brand assets, logos, approved fonts and brand guidelines, product availability, and any other relevant files, in usable quality, correctly labelled where possible, delivered by the agreed monthly content deadlines through a shared folder or other agreed method. House of Musa is responsible for ensuring it has the rights and permissions required for all supplied materials. The monthly pay covers content strategy, creative direction, full content production leadership, planning, coordination, copy and captions, publishing oversight, and review of supplied assets. Full content production is part of this role: the Brand Lead leads and delivers it end to end. Production costs are not included in the monthly pay. Where a production task needs budget to complete it, the Brand Lead will ask House of Musa for that budget first, stating the amount and what it covers, and will not commit or spend production money until the budget is approved in writing. Hands-on video editing is simply not included in the monthly pay. Advanced animation, extensive retouching, complex motion graphics, and unlimited revisions are also not included in the monthly pay.

9. House of Musa responsibilities and approvals. House of Musa will: provide timely access to social accounts, brand materials, product information, and any agreed third-party platforms; supply product images, raw footage, and other content files by the agreed deadlines; provide accurate product descriptions, prices, stock information, shipping and returns details, and customer-service guidance; review and approve calendars, captions, creative concepts, and content within the agreed approval window (two business days where possible, or the timeline agreed for a specific campaign), consolidating feedback through one primary decision-maker; and handle order fulfilment, payment processing, shipping, returns, customer complaints, and other operational matters unless separately agreed. Delays in receiving files, information, or approvals may affect the publishing schedule; the Brand Lead is not responsible for missed deadlines caused by late client materials or approvals.

10. Working arrangements. Work is performed remotely, with communication through agreed channels such as email and a designated messaging platform. Working days are Monday to Friday, and the role averages about 40 hours per week, some weeks less and some weeks more, with the average being what counts. Response windows and any required time-zone overlap will be agreed before commencement and recorded in the Brand Lead’s onboarding. Routine communication and community management take place during agreed working hours; this is not a 24/7 service. One scheduled monthly strategy meeting is included; additional meetings may be arranged by mutual agreement. Urgent, same-day, or out-of-hours requests are subject to availability and may attract an additional fee.

11. Pay and payment terms. House of Musa will pay the Brand Lead ₦560,000 (five hundred sixty thousand naira) per month for the execution of this contract. The monthly amount is payable in advance at the beginning of each billing cycle. Work begins once the agreed scope is confirmed and the initial payment has been received. Fees are quoted in Nigerian naira; if payment is ever to be made in another currency, the invoicing currency, exchange-rate basis, and any transfer charges will be agreed in writing before the first such invoice. Any work outside the agreed scope will be discussed and approved in writing, with the additional fee confirmed before work begins. Third-party costs are not included in the monthly pay.

12. Exclusions and production costs. Full content production leadership is included in this role, as set out in clause 8. The costs of production are not included in the monthly pay and always need a budget approved in advance: studio or location hire, models, photographers, videographers, makeup artists, production crew, props, wardrobe, product shipping, or courier costs. Unless specifically added to this Agreement in writing, the following services are also not included: influencer or talent fees, paid media budgets, advertising spend, or platform fees; website design, development, technical maintenance, e-commerce operations, or customer support beyond agreed social inbox monitoring; product sourcing or purchasing, physical styling on set, travel, and accommodation; hands-on video editing, advanced animation, or extensive graphic design; and full brand identity design, logo design, or a complete rebrand unless separately scoped.

13. Brand audit and other project work. Project-based strategic work, including a full brand audit, brand repositioning, standalone content strategy, website review, or campaign creative direction, is separate from this monthly engagement and is not included in the monthly pay. Any such project, and its fee, will be agreed in writing before the work begins.

14. Term, review, and scope changes. This engagement begins on the start date recorded in the Brand Lead’s onboarding. The first 3 months are the probation period described in clause 3 of this Agreement. The scope, workload, and pay will be reviewed after the first three months, at the end of the probation period, or earlier if the responsibilities materially change. Any increase in platforms, content volume, editing requirements, response coverage, or strategic responsibility may require a revised fee. Either side may propose changes to the scope; changes take effect only after written agreement.

15. Confidentiality and work product. The Brand Lead is bound by the one-way House of Musa Non-Disclosure and Ownership Agreement signed during this onboarding; confidential business information, account access, and unreleased campaign materials are treated as confidential. All work product created under this engagement, including content, calendars, concepts, briefs, and brand materials, is the sole and exclusive property of House of Musa and stays at House of Musa. The Brand Lead may not take, keep, copy, remove, or use any of it, including in a portfolio, during or after the engagement, without written approval from House of Musa.

16. Ending the engagement. Either side may end this engagement with written notice. On ending, the Brand Lead will return or delete House of Musa materials and hand over all work in progress, logins, and files connected to the role, as required by the NDA.

17. Governing law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the District of Columbia, consistent with the House of Musa NDA.

For House of Musa: Omotayo M. Akintoye, Founder.

The runway

Your first 30, 60, 90 days

Your first 90 days follow the house rhythm, shaped around your role: learn the house, own the content engine, then lead the brand world. Progress is reviewed with the founder at each phase, and your scope and pay are formally reviewed at the three month mark under your agreement.

30

Learn the house

  • Download Muse immediately during onboarding, and finish onboarding and set up every tool and account
  • Study the brand: frames, SS01, past campaigns, and the customer journey
  • Settle your working rhythm with your Personal Assistant and meet your team
  • Deliver your first monthly content calendar and content pillars
  • Hold your first monthly strategy and planning meeting

Check in: end of week 1, then at day 30 with the founder.

60

Own the engine

  • Run the full monthly cycle end to end: calendar, concepts, publishing, community
  • Deliver 12 to 16 feed posts and 12 to 20 story updates a month, on schedule
  • Direct your team day to day and review their output before it ships
  • Present your first monthly performance summary with recommendations

Check in: day 60 review against your deliverables.

90

Lead the brand world

  • Lead up to two campaign or shoot concepts a month with styling direction
  • Show measurable movement in positioning, trust, and conversion
  • Own the one year outlook on the next step: holiday content, deal content, and clothing drops planned a quarter ahead
  • Bring one improvement idea for how the house runs its content
  • Scope, workload, and pay review with the founder, per your agreement

Check in: day 90 review and next quarter plan.

The weekly rhythm

Team meeting every Wednesday. Come with what you shipped, what is blocked, and what is next. Day to day questions go in your department WhatsApp group, so the whole team can see the answer.

Ahead of the curve

Your one year outlook

This is the shape of the year ahead, not a locked list of everything that will go out. Products, prices, and exact post dates are firmed up quarter by quarter in your monthly calendar. What this outlook locks is direction and timing, so House of Musa is never planning a holiday, a deal, or a clothing drop at the last minute. It serves the house’s one year plan: a $100K revenue target and one collection drop per quarter.

Your job on this outlook: keep the house at least a quarter ahead of today. Holiday content and deal content go out for every holiday, without exception, and every clothing drop gets a full content runway before it lands. You own this outlook, you review it at every monthly strategy meeting, and you flag clashes, gaps, and missing assets to the founder early, while there is still time to fix them.

Dec 2026 to Feb 2027

Holiday, launch, and gifting

The biggest commercial stretch of the year, and your first quarter in the role.

  • Holiday and deal content leads: Black Friday and the holiday gifting season, with gift guides, worn close ups of the frames, an email for every moment, and the standing monthly deal running alongside.
  • First clothing drop: the clothing line launches with a few select items by December 2026, before the holidays. SS01 leads: the powder blue pinstripe set, the wide leg jeans, tees, and the Timbuktu silk scarf.
  • South Africa launch: December 2026 at the Kickbox store in Johannesburg, with Cape Town content following in early January 2027.
  • Valentine’s Day: product led content and an emailed sale in February 2027, planned in January, not in February.

Mar to May 2027

Spring stories and the second drop

The year settles into its rhythm: one drop, every holiday covered, numbers reviewed.

  • Second quarterly clothing drop: concept and shoot planned during winter, so the spring launch lands on time with its content already made.
  • Mother’s Day: gifting content and a deal in May, with assets ready in April.
  • Spring eyewear stories: new light, travel, and events, with the frames close and clear in every shot and every worn photo linking to the product worn.
  • Reset: review the winter numbers, then reset the content pillars for the rest of the year.

Jun to Aug 2027

Peak sun, peak eyewear

Summer is eyewear season. The calendar leans into it, and holiday planning starts early.

  • Summer content: travel, outdoor, and event stories with the frames as the hero, across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Pinterest.
  • Holiday and deal moments: Father’s Day and Independence Day content and deals, plus the standing monthly promotion and the weekly email.
  • Third quarterly clothing drop: planned in spring, launched in summer.
  • Start the holiday ramp now: Black Friday and gifting concepts are scoped before summer ends, not in November.

Sep to Nov 2027

Fashion season and the holiday ramp

The year closes the way it opened: a drop, the fashion calendar, and the holidays, all planned ahead.

  • Fourth quarterly clothing drop, with Fashion Week season content around it.
  • Fall moments: Labor Day and Halloween content and deals, each planned weeks ahead.
  • Holiday ramp: Black Friday 2027 deal content and the gifting season are built in October, ready before November begins.
  • One year review: what the outlook got right, what it missed, and the next year set out with the founder.

The holiday and deal engine

Every holiday gets the same treatment, every time. This is not optional content: it is a standing part of the calendar, and it is planned like a launch.

  • Content: a product led series across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Pinterest. Holiday ads are product ads, built from existing house content, with the shades front and center.
  • Email: an emailed sale for every holiday, alongside the weekly email. Every email is run by the founder before it sends, so holiday emails are drafted early enough for that review.
  • Deal: one clear offer per holiday, decided in advance, alongside the standing monthly deal or promotion. House offers to know on day one: the 15% welcome offer for new subscribers, and the Black Friday offer of 30% off orders over $200.
  • Timing: each moment is scoped six weeks out, creative is locked two to three weeks out, and nothing holiday related is briefed in the week it goes live.

The holiday list you plan around: Black Friday, the December holidays and gifting season, New Year, Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, and Halloween, plus house moments such as launches, pop ups, and Fashion Week.

How a clothing drop gets planned

One collection drop per quarter, and every drop follows the same runway, starting with the first clothing launch in December 2026. You own the concept, the calendar, and the creative direction; the founder approves the drop plan before the runway starts.

  • 8 weeks out

    Concept. The drop’s story, hero pieces, styling direction, and visual references are set, and the campaign concept goes to the founder.

  • 6 weeks out

    Shoot and assets. Campaign and product assets are shot or gathered, with the frames and garments shown worn, close, and clear.

  • 4 weeks out

    Calendar locked. The content calendar, the launch email, and the deal mechanic, if the drop carries one, are agreed and approved.

  • 2 weeks out

    Teasers. Anticipation content goes out without revealing unreleased product before its time. Unreleased designs stay confidential under your NDA.

  • Launch week

    The drop. Launch content, email, and social go out together, with the product as the hero in every asset.

  • After launch

    Worn and reviewed. Two weeks of worn content and customer moments, then a short performance readout that feeds the planning of the next drop.
